text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.4% today to $388.14, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 2.8% after hitting $424.89 just five trading days earlier. The timing aligns with news on September 23rd that a potential diesel export ban—being weighed by the Trump administration—would actually lead refiners to *cut* production once any initial relief wore off, which directly threatens refinery margins and throughput for a company like this one that makes money by processing crude into fuel.

The broader backdrop adds uncertainty: oil prices themselves are volatile and hard to predict right now given the Iran situation and Middle East tensions, refineries are running at 94% capacity (fairly high but not maxed out), and diesel storage levels remain elevated at 107 million barrels. That combination of policy risk hitting refining economics, geopolitical fog, and already-soft fuel demand appears to have spooked investors over the past week.
